script.stored_text_completeness: All 18998 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("Everything else is just marketing."); ASR/caption artifacts (">> [laughter]", "Melly"); 3,227 words over 1,361 seconds (~142 wpm) is consistent with a full read; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: Two people cross $100,000 on the exact same Friday. Same zip code, same age, same industry. Picture the first one, Chase. He's sitting in his car in the parking lot after work staring at the direct deposit notification, and he actually laughs out loud. Not because he's celebrating, because he spent the drive home mentally adding up what he owes this month, and the number he just got paid still isn't enough. Now, picture the second one, Melly. Same notification,
script.ending_words: people who win it are the ones who figure out early that the goal was never the salary. The goal was always the margin between the salary and the life. The day you feel rich will not arrive because your paycheck got bigger, it will arrive the first Tuesday you realize your expenses didn't grow as fast as your income did. That's the real threshold. Everything else is just marketing.
script.analysis: Full 18998 canonical characters read. A threshold essay: two-earner cold open, inflation erosion of $100,000, six-figure prevalence, tax and phase-outs at $100K, home affordability and metro income requirements, rent burden and HUD low-income limits, a dual-income Parkers budget, paycheck-to-paycheck U-curve, childcare costs and the DCFSA, account limits vs savings capacity, retirement benchmarks, $400 emergency fragility, income-happiness research, and three action items. Verified: 2026 401(k)/IRA/DCFSA limits; federal tax and TX take-home reproduce; 28%-rule $360K reproduces. Wrong: 1980 purchasing power ($25,700 not $36,000); Parkers expenses sum to $10,000 not $12,400; two kids $34,540 not $30,000; DCFSA covers 43% not 29% of the national average; $100K is ~1.9x not 4x median income. Several surveys and metro figures not fetched. The stored ending is complete.

Summary and three action items; close.
